bigIdea: How are plants, animals, and humans connected in different biomes?
readingSkill: Understanding Headings (identifying section topics) & Understanding the Author's Purpose (entertain, inform, or persuade)

reading1.title: Two Different Forests
reading1.summary: This informational text compares deciduous and coniferous forest biomes. Deciduous forests grow across North America, Europe, and China, with four distinct seasons. In autumn, their leaves turn orange, brown, and red before falling to the ground. Animals like bears, raccoons, deer, and squirrels live here, and some hibernate when winter comes and food is scarce. Coniferous forests grow in colder regions with freezing winters reaching -50°C. Coniferous trees have cones and thin evergreen needles instead of broad leaves or flowers. Animals such as hares, lynx, wolves, and owls adapt to the cold and snow by growing thick white fur or feathers for warmth and camouflage.
keySentences: Deciduous trees grow all over the world. They grow in parts of North America, Europe, and China.
We call these forests coniferous because the trees have cones instead of flowers or fruit.
Some of them have thick white fur, not brown fur. This is one way they adapt.

reading2.title: A New Friend
reading2.summary: In this adaptation of a traditional Korean folk tale, kind Go Ne loves the swallows nesting under his family's roof. When a baby bird falls, Go Ne and his father return it safely. In gratitude, the mother swallow gives Go Ne a mysterious gold seed that grows into a giant fruit filled with gold coins. Jealous neighbor Wen Shu deliberately uses a slingshot to injure a swallow so he can get a gold seed too. Go Ne rushes the wounded bird to the vet. Wen Shu feels guilty and follows them, watching Go Ne spend his gold coins to save the bird. Regretful of his actions, Wen Shu leaves a gift to fix Go Ne's roof, and the two boys become friends.
keySentences: Every spring, a swallow built its nest under Go Ne's roof.
After a few weeks, there was a big, round fruit. ... It was full of gold coins. They were rich!
Later that day, Wen Shu went to Go Ne's house. He left a special gift so they could fix the roof.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Why do coniferous trees keep their needles in the winter?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: Their thin, waxy needles survive freezing cold weather without losing moisture, so they stay evergreen all year.

comprehensionQuestions.question: How does the snowshoe hare adapt to winter in the coniferous forest?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: Its fur changes from brown in summer to thick white in winter to blend into the snow and stay warm.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Why do bears hibernate in the deciduous forest during winter?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: Deciduous trees lose their leaves and fruit in autumn, so there is not much food available during winter.

comprehensionQuestions.question: What was the author's main purpose for writing 'Two Different Forests'?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: To inform and teach readers about the differences between deciduous and coniferous forest biomes.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Why did the mother swallow give Go Ne a magical gold seed?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: She was grateful because Go Ne and his father saved her baby bird when it fell out of the nest.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Why did Wen Shu shoot the swallow's nest with his slingshot?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: He was jealous of Go Ne's wealth and wanted to force a swallow to give him a gold seed too.

comprehensionQuestions.question: What important lesson does 'A New Friend' teach about kindness?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: It teaches us to be kind to animals and people, and that if we make a mistake, we should apologize and help fix the problem.

grammarPoints.pattern: Subject + verb + so that / so + subject + can + base verb (Expressing Purpose & Adaptation)
examples: Animals change color in the winter so they can hide in the snow.
Wen Shu left a gift so they could fix the roof.

grammarPoints.pattern: Subject + have/use + [noun A] + instead of + [noun B] (Contrast)
examples: Coniferous trees have cones instead of flowers or fruit.
We used warm wood instead of stone.
A swallow built its nest, and one baby bird fell to the ground.
Go Ne paid the vet with gold coins from the plant.

grammarPoints.pattern: The author wrote this text to + [base verb: teach / entertain / persuade]
examples: The author wrote this article to compare two types of forest.
The author wrote this story to entertain us and teach a lesson.

cultureOrContentFacts: Deciduous trees lose all their broad leaves in autumn, which helps them conserve water through freezing winter months.
Coniferous (taiga/boreal) forests cover vast parts of Canada, Scandinavia, and Siberia where winter temperatures drop below -50°C.
'A New Friend' is a modern retelling of 'Heungbu and Nolbu' (흥부와 놀부), one of Korea's most cherished traditional folk tales about brotherly kindness versus greed.
Swallows (제비) in Korean culture are beloved heralds of spring and symbols of good fortune that return to build nests under human eaves.
In British English, a Y-shaped shooting toy is called a 'catapult', while American English calls it a 'slingshot' (noted on p. 35).

Macro photograph of a woody pine cone nestled in sharp, dark green pine needles, with a round dial thermometer reading -50 degrees Celsius.
Coniferous predators and prey: pure white snowshoe hare mid-leap, spotted Canada lynx, grey wolf portrait, and camouflaged snowy owl.
Traditional Korean village setting with curved tiled roofs, paper doors, and young Go Ne admiring a swallow swooping overhead in spring.
Excited family sawing open a massive ripe golden gourd at a wooden table, revealing sparkling piles of ancient gold coins while neighbor watches.
Wen Shu aiming a wooden slingshot toward swallow nest, and Go Ne gently wrapping the injured fallen chick in a blue cloth inside his bicycle basket.
Doctor in eyeglasses and white coat examining the blue baby swallow while Go Ne and regretful Wen Shu wait closely on a wooden clinic bench.
Go Ne offering gold coins to the smiling vet, and Wen Shu secretly placing a roof repair parcel outside Go Ne's gate in the afternoon sunlight.

difficultyFlags: deciduous vs coniferous: Difficult scientific vocabulary for A1+; use the 'leaf-dropper' vs 'cone-maker' mnemonic with tactile pine cone and leaf realia.
slingshot vs catapult: Clarify US vs UK terminology (slingshot = catapult in Britain) so students are not confused by book notes.
author's purpose: Abstract reading strategy; use simple 3-finger category anchors: 1. Teach/Inform (like science text), 2. Entertain/Fun (like story), 3. Persuade (change mind).
irregular past verbs: Verbs like built, fell, grew, paid, sailed need explicit timeline reinforcement.
